text:
matt: heads up — saw a p99 spike in hosted API around 02:14 UTC last night, p99 +1.4s, p95 +600ms. Notified by pager.

sara: saw it too. queue depth jumped on a couple of frontends, looks correlated with a high token count batch from tenant-42 :thinking_face:

jon: digging traces now. early signal points to a kernel selector fallback to aux-kernel on some nodes. might be a selector regression from last week's rollout.

lee: aux-kernel is slower for long seqs — if batching heuristics grouped long+short we could be suffering head-of-line blocking.

ana: infra-bot shows a burst of requests at 02:13:54 from a single IP-range, rate limiter allowed them through (burst policy = 200). could be noisy neighbor.

matt: can you paste the slice from profiler? look for long memcpy or kernel launch stalls.

jon: profiler snippet:
```
[02:14:00] kernel_select: chosen=aux_kv64, latency=83ms
[02:14:01] launch_wait: 42ms
[02:14:02] kv_cache_evictions: tenant=42 count=128
[02:14:03] batch_coalesce: merged=12 max_seq=4096 mean_seq=118
```

sara: kv_cache_evictions -> tenant-42 kept evicting prefixes, causing repeated priming. that explains repeated long tails.

lee: hmm batching merged 12 requests with max_seq 4096 — that will push some work to aux_kernels. our kernel selection heuristic uses max_seq threshold 2048; looks like a regression bumped threshold to 4096 in the A/B rollout.

ana: infra-bot logs:
<infra-bot> rollout id r-2026-04-09 kernel-selector v2 deployed to 30% at 01:50 UTC

matt: ok rollback plan? can we pin selector to v1 on the problematic shard pool?

jon: I pushed a temporary routing override to force primary-kernel for shard-pool us-west-3 for traffic from tenant-42. initial latency back to baseline for that tenant.

sara: other tenants still show elevated p95 though — looks like noisy neighbor plus global batching growth increased queue depth overall.

lee: short-term mitigation: lower batch_coalesce window (was 30ms -> set to 12ms) and reduce max_merge_size from 16 -> 8. Doing it on canary nodes now.

ana: also reduced burst allowance for the API gateway for the offending IP-range to 20. infra-bot confirms rate-limit update applied at 02:22.

matt: good. next steps: revert kernel-selector v2 rollout and add a regression test for the max_seq threshold so future selector changes can't increase the threshold without perf gating.

jon: filing a perf regression bug with profiling artifacts and a diff of selector change. I'll attach the kv priming traces.

sara: add an eval against our long-seq sampler and noisy-tenant harness too.

lee: note for postmortem — we need a better heuristic: consider both p50/p95 seq distribution in a batch, not only max_seq. mixing one long seq with many short ones kills tail.

ana: infra-bot: incident closed by matt at 02:45 UTC. summary: kernel-selector regression + noisy tenant burst + aggressive batch coalesce -> p95/p99 spike. mitigations: routing override, batch window reduction, rate-limit tighten, rollback rollout.

matt: thanks everyone. I'll draft a short postmortem and action items.
